sentences.text: Some marks don’t tell you which side of a channel to pass.
A safe water mark has red and white vertical stripes, often a red ball topmark, and a white light flashing Morse code A.
It means open water all around, often the start of a channel.
An isolated danger mark is black with red bands, with two black balls on top and a white light flashing in groups of two.
It sits right on a small hazard with navigable water around it.
A preferred channel mark has horizontal bands, and you treat it as the color of its top band.
Yellow special marks show anchorages, cable areas, spoil areas and similar features.
